findings.what: The analogy says low resistance does not make a cable high-rated, but a cable's rating comes from its I²R heat, so a lower resistance per metre does raise it (Dan sizes cables to BS 7671 and will know this), and the mapping is also flipped because stiff means a steep slope, which is high resistance; a resistor's ohms against its power rating (two 100 Ω resistors, one rated 0.25 W and one 50 W) keeps the slope and the limit truly separate, with 'breaks' saying a resistor past its rating burns and keeps nothing like a permanent stretch.
